Person-Item Map (Targeting Plot) for Bayesian IRT Models

Source: R/brms_plots.R
plot_targeting.Rd

Produces a three-panel targeting plot with a shared logit x-axis:

Usage

plot_targeting(
  model,
  item_var = item,
  person_var = id,
  robust = FALSE,
  center = TRUE,
  sort_items = c("data", "location"),
  bins,
  prob = 0.95,
  palette = NULL,
  person_fill = "#0072B2",
  threshold_fill = "#D55E00",
  height_ratios = c(3, 2, 5),
  panel = c("categories", "thresholds"),
  person_estimate = c("eap", "wle"),
  xlim = c(-4, 4),
  category_labels = NULL,
  viridis_option = "G",
  viridis_begin = 0.9,
  viridis_end = 0.2,
  row_gap = NULL,
  output = c("patchwork", "list")
)

Arguments

model

A fitted brmsfit object from an ordinal IRT model (e.g., family = acat) or a dichotomous model (family = bernoulli()).

item_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the item grouping variable in the model data. Default is item.

person_var

An unquoted variable name identifying the person grouping variable in the model data. Default is id.

robust

Logical. If FALSE (the default), the histogram annotations use mean ± SD. If TRUE, median ± MAD is used instead.

center

Logical. If TRUE (the default), the scale is recentred so that the mean of all item threshold locations is zero. Person locations are shifted by the same constant. If FALSE, the raw brms parameterisation is used.

sort_items

Character. How to order items in the bottom panel. "data" (the default) keeps the order in which items first appear in the model data, with the first item at the top. "location" sorts items by their mean threshold location, easiest at the top.

bins

Integer. Number of bins for both histograms. Default is half the maximum possible sum score, rounded up, and at least 11.

prob

Numeric in \((0, 1)\), or NULL. Width of the credible intervals for the item thresholds and of the intervals in the returned categories table. Default is 0.95. NULL hides the threshold intervals in the plot.

palette

An optional character vector of colours, one per response category. Overrides the viridis colours in both panel types.

person_fill

Fill colour for the person histogram. Default is "#0072B2" (blue).

threshold_fill

Fill colour for the threshold histogram, and for the dichotomous dot-and-whisker panel. Default is "#D55E00" (vermillion).

height_ratios

Numeric vector of length 3 giving the relative heights of the top, middle and bottom panels. Default is c(3, 2, 5).

panel

Character. "categories" (the default) draws each item as a bar partitioned into response-category bands, with the threshold estimates and their credible intervals below it. "thresholds" draws a dot-and-whisker plot of the thresholds.

person_estimate

Character. "eap" (the default) uses the posterior means of the person random effects. "wle" uses Warm's weighted likelihood estimates from person_parameters. EAPs are shrunk toward the mean, so their histogram is narrower than that of the WLEs.

xlim

Numeric vector of length 2. Initial limits of the shared x-axis, widened to whole numbers if any person location, threshold or interval falls outside. Default is c(-4, 4).

category_labels

Optional character vector of labels for the response categories, in ascending order and one per category. Used in the legend of the "categories" panel. Default NULL uses the category scores, starting at 0.

viridis_option

Character. Viridis palette option for the category colours. Default is "G" (mako).

viridis_begin, viridis_end

Numeric in \([0, 1]\). Start and end of the viridis palette. Defaults 0.9 and 0.2 run from light to dark, so higher categories are darker.

row_gap

Numeric. Vertical spacing between item rows in the "categories" panel. Default NULL uses 1, widened when a category collapses or thresholds are reversed, to make room for their labels.

output

Character. "patchwork" (the default) returns the combined plot. "list" returns the three panels and the posterior summaries of the category structure.

Value

With output = "patchwork", a patchwork object. With output = "list", a list with:

p1, p2, p3

The person histogram, threshold histogram and bottom panel as ggplot objects.

categories

A tibble with one row per item and response category: p_never_modal, the posterior probability that the category is never the most likely response at any location, and lower_bound, lower_bound_lo, lower_bound_hi, the posterior median and prob interval of the location where the category starts to be the most likely response, over the draws where it is (NA for category 0).

reversals

A tibble with one row per item and adjacent threshold pair: p_reversed, the posterior probability that the higher threshold lies below the lower one.

Details

  1. Top: Histogram of person locations, with a reference line for the mean (or median) and shading for ±1 SD (or ±1 MAD).

  2. Middle: Inverted histogram of item threshold locations, with the same summary annotations.

  3. Bottom: One bar per item, either partitioned into response-category bands (panel = "categories", the default) or drawn as a dot-and-whisker plot of the individual thresholds (panel = "thresholds").

Together, the top and middle panels form a back-to-back histogram that shows whether the test is well targeted to the sample. The bottom panel places the items on the same scale, so the category bands show which response is the most likely one at the locations where the persons are. The layout follows easyRasch2::RMtargeting().

Item thresholds come from the posterior draws (see item_parameters). Points are posterior means and intervals are equal-tailed credible intervals.

Category bands. With panel = "categories", each band spans the locations at which its response category is the most likely response, computed from the posterior mean thresholds. When an item's thresholds are ordered these boundaries are the thresholds themselves. When they are not, the disordered run is pooled by averaging, and the categories it skips over, which are never the most likely response at any location, collapse to a red tick labelled with the category number. Red arrows below the bar give the size of each threshold reversal in logits. The two outer bands fade towards the panel edge, since they are open-ended.

Posterior probabilities. The same category structure is computed for every posterior draw. Each red tick is labelled with the posterior probability that its category is never the most likely response, and each reversal with the posterior probability that the pair is reversed. The full tables, including categories and pairs without red marks, are returned with output = "list".

Person locations. person_estimate = "eap" uses the posterior means of the person random effects, shifted by the same constant as the thresholds. "wle" uses the WLEs of person_parameters, which are finite at extreme scores and use the items each person answered.

References

Wright, B. D. & Stone, M. H. (1979). Best Test Design. MESA Press.

Bürkner, P.-C. (2021). Bayesian Item Response Modeling in R with brms and Stan. Journal of Statistical Software, 100, 1–54. doi:10.18637/jss.v100.i05

See also

plot_ipf for item category probability curves, item_parameters, person_parameters.

Examples

# \donttest{
library(brms)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

# --- Partial Credit Model ---

df_pcm <- eRm::pcmdat2 %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~ .x + 1)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("id") %>%
  pivot_longer(!id, names_to = "item", values_to = "response")

fit_pcm <- brm(
  response | thres(gr = item) ~ 1 + (1 | id),
  data   = df_pcm,
  family = acat,
  chains = 4,
  cores  = 1, # use more cores if you have
  iter   = 500 # use at least 2000
)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Error in .fun(model_code = .x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')

# Default: category bands, EAP person locations, items in data order
plot_targeting(fit_pcm)
#> Error: object 'fit_pcm' not found

# WLE person locations, items sorted by location, labelled categories
plot_targeting(fit_pcm, person_estimate = "wle", sort_items = "location",
               category_labels = c("Never", "Sometimes", "Often"))
#> Error: object 'fit_pcm' not found

# Dot-and-whisker panel
plot_targeting(fit_pcm, panel = "thresholds")
#> Error: object 'fit_pcm' not found

# Panels and posterior summaries of the category structure
res <- plot_targeting(fit_pcm, output = "list")
#> Error: object 'fit_pcm' not found
res$categories
#> Error: object 'res' not found
res$reversals
#> Error: object 'res' not found

# --- Dichotomous Rasch Model ---

df_rm <- eRm::raschdat3 %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column("id") %>%
  pivot_longer(!id, names_to = "item", values_to = "response")

fit_rm <- brm(
  response ~ 1 + (1 | item) + (1 | id),
  data   = df_rm,
  family = bernoulli(),
  chains = 4,
  cores  = 1, # use more cores if you have
  iter   = 500 # use at least 2000
)
#> Compiling Stan program...
#> Error in .fun(model_code = .x1): Boost not found; call install.packages('BH')

plot_targeting(fit_rm, sort_items = "location")
#> Error: object 'fit_rm' not found
# }
